C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S607C

SPONSOR: STAVISKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law and the social services law, in
relation to the licensure of dietitians and nutritionists; and to repeal
certain provisions of the education law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To establish licensure for dietitians and nutritionists in New York
State and create a protected scope of practice for licensed profes-
sionals providing medical nutrition therapy and nutrition care services.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends section 8000 of the education law to
replace the current certification structure with licensure for licensed
dietitians and licensed nutritionists and clarifies that licensed
professionals may provide medical nutrition therapy within the scope of
their training and experience.

Section 2 amends section 8001 of the education law to define the prac-
tice of dietetics and nutrition and establish that licensed profes-
sionals may provide medical nutrition therapy, advanced medical nutri-
tion therapy, nutrition counseling, nutrition assessment, therapeutic
diets, and chronic disease management services in inpatient, outpatient,
and telehealth settings.

Section 3 amends section 8002 of the education law to establish title
protections for "Licensed Dietitian," "Licensed Nutritionist," and
related abbreviations and prohibits unauthorized individuals from using
such titles.

Section 4 adds a new section 8002-a to the education law defining terms
including advanced medical nutrition therapy, medical nutrition therapy,
nutrition care services, nutrition diagnosis, and therapeutic diets.

Section 5 amends section 8003 of the education law relating to the State
Board for Dietetics and Nutrition and updates board composition require-
ments, including representation from licensed dietitians, licensed
nutritionists, public members, and a physician member.

Section 6 repeals and replaces section 8004 of the education law to
establish licensure requirements for licensed nutritionists and licensed
dietitians, including education, supervised practice experience, exam-
inations, registration requirements, and fees.

Section 7 repeals section 8005 of the education law.

Section 8 repeals and replaces section 8006 of the education law to
establish transition and grandfathering provisions allowing currently
certified dietitians and certified nutritionists to become licensed
under specified conditions.

Section 9 adds new sections 8007 and 8008 to the education law estab-
lishing exemptions and limited permit provisions for certain healthcare

professionals, students, trainees, federal employees, WIC employees,
supervised personnel, and other specified individuals and entities.

Section 10 amends section 6503-a of the education law to make conforming
changes relating to professions requiring licensure.

Section 11 amends section 6505-b of the education law to require
licensed nutritionists and licensed dietitians to complete infection
control coursework and training requirements.

Section 12 amends section 6507 of the education law to require licensed
nutritionists and licensed dietitians to complete coursework relating to
the identification and reporting of child abuse and maltreatment.

Section 13 amends section 413 of the social services law to include
licensed nutritionists and licensed dietitians among mandated reporters
of child abuse and maltreatment.

Section 14 amends section 488 of the social services law to include
licensed nutritionists and licensed dietitians within the definition of
"human services professional."

Section 15 establishes an effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Current New York State law allows dietitians and nutritionists to obtain
title certification through the State Education Department.  However,
while certification protects the use of certain professional titles, it
does not adequately protect the actual scope of practice relating to
medical nutrition therapy and nutrition care services.  Under current
law, individuals without sufficient education, supervised clinical expe-
rience, or competency standards may still provide therapeutic diet
services and nutrition treatment so long as they do not use protected
certified titles.

This legislation modernizes New York's regulation of dietetics and
nutrition by transitioning from certification to licensure for qualified
professionals. The bill establishes clear standards for education,
supervised practice, examination, and professional competency for indi-
viduals providing medical nutrition therapy and advanced nutrition care
services.

The legislation also clarifies the distinct roles and qualifications of
licensed dietitians and licensed nutritionists while preserving
exemptions for general wellness information, non-medical nutrition guid-
ance, and other permitted activities outside the licensed scope of prac-
tice. Additionally, the bill updates professional oversight requirements
and aligns New York's standards more closely with nationally recognized
professional and healthcare standards.

Licensure will help ensure that individuals providing medical nutrition
therapy, nutrition care services, and therapeutic diet treatment possess
the appropriate education, training, and clinical competency necessary
to safely treat patients and improve public health outcomes across New
York State.


The bill further strengthens consumer protections by establishing clear-
er professional accountability standards and ensuring that patientS
receiving nutrition-related medical care are treated by appropriately
qualified and regulated professionals.
